claim: Wallas's four stages (preparation, incubation, illumination, verification) were derived from introspective anecdotes (Helmholtz, Poincare), not experiments; the sources checked report no experimental test of the stage order as a causal sequence.
agent_test: Compare an agent forced through fixed stage order against one with free state choice at equal tokens.
audit_note: Wallas text (Art of Thought 1926, Helmholtz and Poincare as worked cases, Intimation, four stages) confirmed, but 'no effect size supports the stage order as a causal sequence' is an absence claim no opened source tests (the EEG paper only lists stage models).
claim_before_audit: Wallas's four stages (preparation, incubation, illumination, verification) come from anecdotes (Helmholtz, Poincare), not experiments; no effect size supports the stage order as a causal sequence.

claim: Lab incubation gives a small positive average effect on problem solving: 117 studies, 85 positive, mean d about 0.29 to 0.41 (weighted vs unweighted figures differ between sources), with large heterogeneity and median N 25.
agent_test: Meta-level only; use as prior that any break step gives a small, noisy gain.
audit_note: Sio and Ormerod 2009 confirmed directly (117 studies, 85 positive, N 3606, median 25, unweighted d .41, weighted .29, Q significant); Gilhooly 2016 only re-cites the same meta-analysis, so effectively one source.

claim: Incubation effects grow with longer preparation before the break (r = .40 visual, .60 creative) and are larger for divergent/creative tasks than for insight puzzles.
agent_test: Vary pre-break effort (1k vs 4k tokens) then run a pause step; compare gain on stuck items.

claim: Filling the break with a low-demand task beats rest on linguistic insight problems; high-demand fillers reduce the effect.
agent_test: Test an unrelated low-load filler generation vs no filler between attempts.

claim: Immediate incubation (break before starting) can help divergent thinking more than delayed incubation (break after work), supporting unconscious work over rest.
agent_test: Insert a pause plus a different task before the first attempt vs after a failed attempt.

claim: The unconscious thought advantage is not robust: meta-analysis g = 0.15, trim-and-fill g = 0.018 [-0.10, 0.14] with funnel asymmetry; a large preregistered replication (N = 399) found no advantage, BF 7.83 for the null; a second meta (17 contrasts) z = 0.35, p = .73.
schema_part: none (do not add an unconscious-thought stage)
agent_test: Compare deliberate extended reasoning vs a distraction-filler step on multi-option choice tasks.
audit_note: All figures (g .15, trim-and-fill .018 [-.10,.14], Z=2.11, N=399, BF 7.83, 17 contrasts z=.35 p=.73) match Nieuwenstein 2015 and the medical-decision meta-analysis; the two JDM entries are one paper.

claim: Delay can help by dropping misleading fixation: Smith and Beda found incubation F(1,142)=22.86 and new-context gains (d about .19 to .22 in delayed retest), replicated, but the context x incubation interaction was not significant in either experiment.
agent_test: After failing, discard the failed context and restart from only the problem statement; compare with continuing in context.

claim: Mind wandering during a break predicting incubation gain (Baird 2012) has failed to replicate in several labs (Smeekens and Kane, Steindorf, Murray) with null effects at 0-back accuracy near .91 to .93.
agent_test: Not testable directly; skip mind-wandering analogues such as random drift text.

claim: Mind-wandering diversity and mindfulness effects on incubation are small-sample and subgroup-dependent (r = .40 in one subgroup of 29; tau = .28 at N = 28).
agent_test: Low priority.

claim: Sleep, especially sleep onset (N1), raised hidden-rule discovery: Wagner 2004 more than twice as many after sleep (about 60% vs 23%); Lacaux 2021 N1 83% vs wake 30%, N2 14%.
agent_test: Offline replay or rewrite of a notebook between sessions, compared at equal tokens to continued work.
audit_note: Lacaux 2021 numbers match exactly (N1 83.33% 20/24, wake 30.61%, N2 14.29%); Wagner 2004 abstract confirms 'more than twice as many' after sleep (the 60% vs 23% figures are not in the abstract and were not independently opened); note a 2025 preregistered nap study (Lowe et al.) found N2 not N1 raised insight, so the N1 emphasis is contested.

claim: Sleep benefit is not universal: a 2026 REM study found no difference (wake 20%, NREM 5%, REM 11.4%, p = .36), targeted memory reactivation added nothing beyond sleep (56 to 58% vs 57%), and benefits depend on problem difficulty.
agent_test: None; boundary condition for any offline-consolidation claim.

claim: Interactivity during the break matters: external chains raised Time-1 solving (43% vs 6%) and Time-2 gain among failures (44% vs 15%), so externalising state aids insight.
agent_test: Give the agent an editable scratchpad vs none on insight puzzles.

claim: Sleep-time compute (precomputing about a context before the query) cuts test-time compute about 5x at equal accuracy, adds up to +13% and +18% accuracy with scaling, and 2.5x lower cost per query when amortised; gain tracks query predictability. Gap search: the gain is conditional. At high test-time budgets test-time-only slightly wins (GPT-4o family), and o1 gained little.
agent_test: Offline summarisation of context vs none at equal total tokens, split by predictable vs unpredictable questions.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-20 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Sleep-time compute helps less on a realistic agentic SWE task: about 1.5x fewer tokens only at low budget; at high test-time budget test-time-only had higher precision.
agent_test: Replicate on our coding tasks across budgets.

claim: Appending 'Wait' (budget forcing) to extend thinking moved s1-32B from 50% to 57% on AIME24; Wait beat other strings; but longer budgets can backtrack and hurt.
agent_test: Compare Wait-style continuation vs independent resampling at equal tokens.
audit_note: s1 abstract (50% to 57% AIME24), Wait-beats-other-strings ablation and backtracking/inverse-scaling remark in rejection sampling confirmed; Ghosal 2025 independently shows Wait-and-Think-More hurting at long budgets; the 57% is the rounded 56.7.

claim: Longer reasoning is non-monotonic: accuracy rises then falls (82.2 to 87.3 to 70.3%), parallel thinking beats sequential extension by up to 20%, and inverse scaling appears on distractor tasks.
schema_part: G: budget caps; O: parallel sampling
agent_test: Equal-token sweep of sequential thinking length against best-of-N with majority vote.
audit_note: Ghosal 2025 numbers (82.2->87.3->70.3, up to 20% in abstract, 22%/47% in text) and Gema 2025 inverse-scaling distractor family match; sources are independent labs.

claim: Frequent thought switching is a failure mode: wrong AIME answers use 225% more tokens and 418% more switches; a decoding penalty raised pass@1 (QwQ 38.3 to 44.1) but a prompt-only version did not.
schema_part: G: stay on a line of attack
agent_test: Switch-penalty vs none at equal tokens; count line changes.

claim: Intrinsic self-correction without external feedback does not help and often hurts (GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1; GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 89.0); it helps only with oracle signals.
agent_test: Self-review round vs verifier-gated revision at equal tokens.
audit_note: Huang 2024 Table: GPT-3.5 CSQA 75.8->38.1 (round 2 five calls 41.8), GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5->89.0, oracle labels needed; 'only' is slightly strong but the paper says improvements vanish without oracle labels.

claim: Structured search and reflection in agents beat plain chain-of-thought: Tree of Thoughts 74% vs 4% on Game of 24; reflection ablations add measurable believability and +8% on Reflexion.
agent_test: Branching with an evaluator vs single chain at equal tokens.
audit_note: ToT 74% vs 4%, Reflexion +8% absolute over episodic memory (HotPotQA CoT(GT) ablation) and Park believability 29.89 vs 26.88 all match.

claim: LLMs show human-like behaviour on insight problem sets and exceed average humans on divergent tasks (Hedges g 0.5 to 2.6), but lateral thinking puzzles remain hard (BRAINTEASER sentence puzzles ChatGPT about 61% vs human 91%).
agent_test: Not an incubation test; use as baseline for a divergence step.

claim: No study found tests human-style incubation (set aside, then return) as a deliberate LLM scaffold step; closest analogues are sleep-time compute, Wait continuation and DreamCoder sleep.
agent_test: Abandon after failure, run an unrelated filler, return with fresh context; compare with a continued attempt.

claim: Offline (sleep-time) compute pays off in proportion to how predictable the later query is from the context; for unpredictable queries the benefit shrinks, and at large test-time budgets or on agentic SWE tasks test-time-only matches or wins.
schema_part: idle pass only when next question is predictable
agent_test: Bin held-out items by predictability of the follow-up; compare offline pass vs same tokens at test time per bin.

claim: Plain resampling from scratch can stall on items already failed (Reflexion baselines at temperature 0.7 solved none of their first-trial HotPotQA failures), while carrying a short written lesson helped (+8% absolute over episodic memory alone); but on math at equal 16K tokens independent restarts with voting beat Wait-style continuation by up to 22%.
schema_part: O: restart with distilled lesson, not full failed context
agent_test: On failed items, compare (a) fresh resample, (b) fresh start plus 2-line lesson, (c) Wait continuation, all at equal tokens.

claim: A return-to-problem step needs an external signal that the problem is still unsolved. Self-reflection without oracle labels or tests did not help or hurt (GPT-3.5 keeps 74.7% of GSM8K answers; Rust Reflexion without tests 52% vs 60% baseline), so cheap internal impasse detection is unsolved.
schema_part: G: verifier or test before any retry
agent_test: Trigger retries by test failure vs by self-reported doubt; compare net fixes minus new breaks.
audit_note: Huang 2024 (74.7% kept, improvements vanish without oracle labels) and Reflexion Rust 52% vs 60% match; wording 'did not help or hurt' is ambiguous (it did hurt on Rust), and 'cheap internal impasse detection is unsolved' is an inference.

claim: Reasoning models show an LLM analogue of fixation: R1 ruminates on earlier formulations, and longer reasoning degrades accuracy on distractor, spurious-feature and deduction tasks. No paper tested whether a context reset reverses it, so the Smith/Beda forgetting mechanism has no LLM test.
agent_test: Same stuck items: continue in place vs restart with only the problem statement and constraints, equal tokens.

claim: No source open this session gives a weighted vs unweighted Sio and Ormerod mean d or exact moderator effects; K02 stays a range.
agent_test: Open the APA PDF and extract Table values.
